prompts.title: Prompts
prompts.desc: A versioned prompt library. Paste a prompt, see how it measures against prompting best practices, and watch the score move as you improve it.

tuning.intro: Set the constraints, then ask for a rewrite. These knobs are compiled into instructions for the model — they are not applied to your text mechanically.
tuning.footnote: The rewrite starts from the deterministic findings, so the model spends its effort fixing them rather than rediscovering them.
tuning.requested: Rewrite requested. It will appear under Suggestions.
tuning.sensitivity_hint: How delicate the subject matter is.
tuning.verbosity_hint: How much detail the answer should carry.
tuning.keywords_hint: Enter or comma to add; backspace removes the last one.
tuning.disclaimer_hint: Ask the prompt to caveat its own output.
tuning.disclaimer_text_placeholder: Leave blank for a sensible default

suggestions.empty_body: Set the knobs on the Tuning tab and ask for a rewrite. It runs as an engine job, so you can leave the page.
suggestions.running_hint: {{model}} is working on it. This page updates itself when it lands.
suggestions.failed_generic: The model did not return a usable prompt.
suggestions.identical: The model returned the prompt unchanged.
suggestions.legend: Additions are highlighted, removals struck through. Click any change to reject it — rejected changes dim and keep the original wording.
suggestions.note_all: Accepted the model's rewrite in full.

list.empty_body: Add your first prompt to get an instant read on its clarity, structure and size — no model call needed.

new.title: New prompt
new.desc: The body you paste becomes version 1 and is scored immediately.

form.name: Name
form.guidance_hint: How you want this prompt changed. Kept with the version; used when you ask for a rewrite.

editor.guidance_placeholder: Make it sharper, drop the shouting, keep the reasons
editor.body_placeholder: Paste or write the prompt here
editor.estimate_caveat: Token count is an estimate (about +/-15% on prose, wider on code and JSON). Exact counts come from a real run.
editor.note_placeholder: Added audience and an output shape

checks.empty: Write a prompt to see the checks.
checks.scoring_note: These checks are mechanical: they read the text and never call a model, so they are free, instant and identical every time. Length on its own is not a defect — a rule only fires on something it can name.
checks.clean_body: None of the checks fired. That means no known anti-pattern is present, not that the prompt is perfect.

review.title: Model review
review.caveat: These are one model's judgement on one run, so they move a little between runs. The model that produced them is shown above. The checks above are facts about the text; these are an opinion about it.
review.running: {{model}} is scoring this version. The page updates itself when it lands.
review.empty: Not scored yet. The deterministic checks above are free; this one costs a model call.

versions.trend_hint: Versions are immutable. Making an earlier one current moves the pointer — nothing is deleted, so the history stays honest.

arena.intro: Run this prompt against several models at once and have a separate model judge the answers. Token counts here are measured from the real call, not estimated.
arena.judge: Have a separate model judge the answers
arena.started: Runs queued. They execute in parallel.
arena.concurrency_hint: The engine runs a limited number of jobs at once (Jobs -> Config). Above that, runs queue rather than failing.
arena.empty_body: Pick the models you care about and run. Each answer comes back with its real input and output token counts.

dashboard.up_is_better: Up is better on every line
dashboard.no_runs_yet: Only the deterministic score is plotted so far. Score a version on the Checks tab and run it in the Arena to fill in the other lines.
dashboard.mixed_note: The static score is mechanical; the AI lines are one model's judgement per version and will wobble a little between runs.
dashboard.measured_hint: mean of {{count}} run(s), incl. CLI overhead
